candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis II.2 (NPNF S2 V13). PD.

Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 362 AD)

On 'God ended His work which He had made; and He rested on the seventh day' Ephrem reads the rest (the Syriac 'ettnih) not as cessation from activity (God's providential governance never pauses) but as the establishment of the Sabbath pattern — the divine ordering of time into work-and-rest. The seventh-day rest is therefore not God's exhaustion but God's instructional gift: humans are taught their own work-rhythm by divine example. Ephrem connects this with the eschatological Sabbath-rest awaited by the faithful (cf. Heb 4:9 sabbatismos): the weekly rest typifies the eternal rest, and the eternal rest fulfills the weekly. The Tewahedo Sabbath observance (preserving the Saturday observance alongside Sunday Eucharist) traces its theological warrant to this Ephremic reading.
